To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

4-aryl-6-azidocinolines were efficiently prepared and found to react with terminal alkynes in CuAAC and SPAAC to give corresponding 4-triazole-6-aryl-cinnolines. 4-Triazolylcnnolines were shown to be non-fluorescent.
we developed an efficient approach to 6-aryl-cinnoline-4-azides which can be further transformed into 6-aryl-triazolyl-cinnoline derivatives.
we developed a simple and efficient synthetic route to 4-azidophenylcinnolones and explored their photophysical properties and click chemistry.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a convenient synthesis and properties of 6-(4-bromophenyl)-4-azidobenzo[c]cinnoline, 6-(4-ethoxyphenyl)-4- azidobenzo [c]cinnoline and their derivatives.

the development of a novel and efficient synthetic approach towards 6-aryl-cinnoline-4-azides and 6-aryl-triazolyl-cinnoline derivatives, which are potentially useful as fluorescent dyes and as cytotoxic agents.
a new synthetic approach to the synthesis of 4-azidobenzocinolines.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a combination of 6-arylcinoline core and triazole ring in the 4-position leads to a new class of fluorescent probes for bioconjugation.
6-aryl-cinnolin-4-ones and their azide analogues were synthesized and their photophysical properties were studied.

the 6-aryl cinnoline scaffold with an azide or triazole substituent in the 4-position is a promising platform for the design of novel fluorescent probes for the detection of reactive oxygen species, as well as for the design of cytotoxic agents.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
6-aryl cinnolines are a new class of compounds with potential applications in photodynamic therapy (PDT) and as cytotoxic drugs.
6-aryl-cinnolines bearing an electron-donating group on aryl moiety are suitable for the synthesis of fluorescent 4-(1,3-dipolar cycloadducts) via CuAAC or SPAAC.
we have found a new class of compounds that are fluorescent in their precursor form and are converted by click chemistry into non-fluorescent compounds.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the synthesis of 4-triaryl-4H-cinnoline-1-azides is possible and their photophysical properties can be tuned by the substitution of the triazole ring.
4-triazole-substituted cinnolines can be synthesized in one-pot reaction from readily available 2-ethinyl-4-aryltriazenes.
6-aryl-cinnolines are a promising class of compounds for the development of new fluorescent probes for bioimaging and fluorescent dyes for optical encoding of biological materials.
